validity.recommendation: No action on existence/duplicate/classification for P2353 itself. It is the genuine, physically distinct Phase II segment of the Power of Siberia system (Kovyktinskoye field, Irkutsk Oblast -> Chayandinskoye field, Sakha Republic, ~800-804 km, operating since Dec 21, 2022) and is clearly distinguishable from its named-family siblings: P2352 is Phase I (Chayandinskoye NGKM, Sakha Republic -> Blagoveshchensk, Amur Oblast, ~2,200 km, operating since Dec 2, 2019 -- upstream of and physically prior to this segment); P3208, per an independent technical-library phase breakdown (neftegaz.ru tech-library), corresponds to a Phase III COMPRESSOR-STATION-ONLY capacity expansion along the Chayandinskoye-to-Atamanskaya section of P2352's OWN corridor (7 new compressor stations, 481 MW, target by 2022) -- i.e. not a third physical pipe segment overlapping this row, and not resolved here since it is P3208's own audit; P5521 (Belogorsk-Khabarovsk) and any Power-of-Siberia-2/'Sila Baikala' rows are later, physically separate, not-yet-complete corridors connecting the Power of Siberia system to the unrelated Sakhalin-Khabarovsk-Vladivostok system, unrelated to P2353's own route. No indication P2353 duplicates, or is duplicated by, any other roster row. The prokhab.ru gem.wiki citation (Khabarovsk-Amur Oblast, ~800 km, Oct 2022) found among P2353's wiki citations is NOT relevant to this row -- its termini (Khabarovsk / Amur Oblast) do not match P2353's actual route (Irkutsk Oblast / Sakha Republic); the coincidental '~800 km' figure is the only overlap. Routed as a cross_row_lead for whichever PID actually covers a Khabarovsk-area line (candidate: P5521 or a sibling not in this roster slice) rather than used here.
